new_page.title: Can Foreigners Buy a Home in BC? Federal Ban & 20% Foreign Buyer Tax
new_page.h1: Can foreigners buy a home in BC?
new_page.description: The federal ban on non-Canadians buying homes is set to end January 1, 2027. In the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver, foreign buyers also pay an extra 20% tax.

breadcrumbs.name: Can foreigners buy a home in BC?

faq.q: Do permanent residents pay the foreign buyer tax?
faq.a: No. Canadian citizens and permanent residents do not pay the additional 20% tax.

faq.q: Does the foreign buyer tax apply to farmland?
faq.a: The 20% tax applies to the residential portion of a property. Farmland has its own rules, covered in the farmland guide below.

parts.t: For now, mostly not. A federal law bars most non-Canadians from buying residential property, and it is set to expire on January 1, 2027. On top of that, BC charges foreign buyers an additional 20% property transfer tax on residential property in the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver.

The Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act took effect in 2023 and was extended to January 1, 2027. It has exceptions, for example for some temporary workers and for spouses of Canadians. Whether it is extended again was not announced when this page was checked, so confirm with a lawyer before you make plans.

Foreign nationals, foreign corporations and taxable trustees pay 20% of the residential value, on top of the regular property transfer tax, in the Fraser Valley, Metro Vancouver, Capital, Central Okanagan and Nanaimo regional districts. On a $1,000,000 home that is $200,000 extra, plus $18,000 of regular tax.
Foreign owners who keep a home in a taxable area also pay the speculation and vacancy tax: 3% of assessed value in 2026, rising to 4% in 2027, unless an exemption applies.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
